verdict.rationale: Windmill's first-party docs describe open-source self-hosting of the core product: Docker Compose for single-instance setups and a Helm chart for Kubernetes production deployments. Independent community reports confirm it in practice, with users self-hosting via Caprover one-click install and via Podman plus Docker Compose on Alpine. The product's own llms.txt and intro docs also describe it as open-source and self-hostable.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: For small setups, use Docker and Docker Compose on a single instance. For larger and production use-cases, use our Helm chart to deploy on Kubernetes.
Windmill is an open-source and self-hostable workflow engine and developer platform
Pretty easy to selfhost as I deployed it on a Alpine Linux server using Podman + Docker Compose binary.
Yesterday I submitted a one-click install to Caprover, never been so easy to self host.
